Ronnestad and colleagues (197) found that hypertrophy of the elbow flexors was magnified when training these muscles was preceded by lower-body exercise, ostensibly as a result of an increase in post-exercise hormonal elevations. These results are in contrast to those of West and colleagues (268), who showed that performing lower-body exercise after arm training did not amplify elbow flexor hypertrophy. The disparate findings between these studies call into question whether there is a hypertrophic advantage to performing lower-body exercise before upper-body exercise.
